notes.text: The page is a handwritten working sheet. Cor is underlined above a crossed capital at the opening. Déf is underlined at the lower section. The lower-left pale pencil number is 36; it is retained only as an archive-sheet comment. No separate author page number, date or general title is visible.

The opening corollary uses Card followed by empty braces and 4. Its added upper clause reads et Sigma-one-minus neq X, Sigma-two-minus neq X. The displayed list labelled (*) contains the two written cross inclusions. The empty braces are retained exactly; no elements are supplied.

The left note begins “Sous forme :” and reformulates the preceding text. It includes a doubtful strictes, the visible (*) label, a list of four Sigma terms, the abbreviations “il f et s.”, and the small interlinear mutlt. The final index in its four-term list remains 1/2; the list pattern was not used to replace the first stroke-based reading.

The proof begins “En effet” and successively discusses inverse inclusions, the two inclusions between the same indexed pair, the pair of positive Sigma terms, and the remaining negative-Sigma inclusion. Its own phrase “Il reste à voir” introduces that remaining step. “Disjoints et neq emptyset” and the written “de =” are retained. The nearby unambiguous inclusion bowls were used only as handwriting comparisons for the crowded second operator.

The final proof paragraph refers to “le diagramme (14)”; this page contains that textual reference, without a diagram drawing. The interlinear la première p.ex. is attached over live signifierait que. The earlier Sigma-twelve simeq Sigma-one-minus formula and the short next-line connector are crossed. The live conclusion is Sigma-two-minus = X, followed by “ce que l’on a exclu”. No additional implique is visible.

The definition uses the underlined words “strictement non panachées”, with two uncertain punctuation dots after non at the line break. Its interlinear addition reads “si elles sont non panachées, et”. The common l of a rewritten les is visible once; the possible old low es is retained locally. The passage following distincts contains a doubtful et./i.e. and two open curves before de plus.

The final line is labelled (21). It includes the two Sigma-minus non-equalities with X, the parenthesis “on dit donc que” with underlined propres, and E-one neq Sigma-twelve, E-two neq Sigma-twelve. The last subscript and terminal point lie close to the physical lower/right boundary but are represented. The visible capital E bodies and low indices were read from this page.

All mathematical cues were used to detect places needing inspection, never to supply missing glyphs. In particular the pattern of pair indices did not settle the margin’s last numeral or the hooked Sigma after puisque; the latter high mark is T-shaped in the crop. No proof check, independent re-proof, computation or external verification was performed.
